description:
Hi everyone !

I am a young participant in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, and I am working on a project aimed at developing software to monitor astronauts’ health during space missions.

I am interested in space exploration, new technologies, science, and innovation. My goal is to make space missions safer by developing tools that help monitor astronauts’ health.
summary:
COSMO HEALTH is an offline-ready, zero-dependency crew health monitoring console designed for deep-space missions when Earth communication links are delayed or unavailable. Built as a self-contained single-file web application, it addresses the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge by providing autonomous, explainable onboard triage.

The console monitors four core channels—heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), sleep duration, and local radiation indicators—across 10 interactive mission scenarios and a custom telemetry lab. Instead of opaque algorithms, COSMO HEALTH uses a transparent 6-level rule engine that explains every alert, logs operator acknowledgments, exports session telemetry (JSON/CSV), and explicitly isolates sensor dropouts ("Telemetry unavailable") from medical anomalies so crews never confuse hardware loss with health status. It also embeds published NASA NTRS (20230003916) Standard Measures sleep research across 19 astronauts as an offline scientific benchmark.

As human missions venture beyond low-Earth orbit to the Moon and Mars, real-time ground medical support becomes impossible. COSMO HEALTH empowers crews with clear, reliable, and auditable health situational awareness when autonomy matters most.
details:
### What It Does & How It Works

COSMO HEALTH is a self-contained, offline-ready crew health monitoring console built for deep-space missions when Earth communication links are delayed or unavailable[cite: 1]. Running entirely in a local browser with zero network dependencies, the console tracks four core telemetry channels: Heart Rate (BPM), Oxygen Saturation (% SpO₂), Last Sleep Duration (hours), and a Local Dosimeter indicator (arbitrary demo units)[cite: 1].

At its core is a deterministic, explainable 6-level triage engine (01 Optimal, 02 Nominal, 03 Watch, 04 Caution, 05 Urgent, and 06 Telemetry Unavailable)[cite: 1]. Rather than displaying opaque scores, the console explains the exact rule or mission context behind every alert and suggests an immediate crew action[cite: 1]. Operators can explore 10 built-in mission scenarios—ranging from nominal wake-up (SCN-01) and cumulative sleep debt (SCN-03) to radiation events (SCN-07), oxygen anomalies (SCN-09), and sensor signal loss (SCN-10)—or launch an automated 10-scenario tour at 1×, 2×, or 4× replay speeds[cite: 1]. An interactive Telemetry Lab also lets users inject custom physiological values or simulate sudden sensor disconnection on demand[cite: 1].

To support onboard record-keeping, COSMO HEALTH includes an event acknowledgment workflow (logging crew review without prematurely clearing active alerts), a live mission log (retaining up to 300 events), a 60-sample real-time waveform chart, and one-click local exports in JSON (up to 3,600 samples plus embedded NASA research metadata) and CSV formats[cite: 1]. Furthermore, the console embeds published aggregate sleep data from NASA NTRS (Document 20230003916) across 19 crew members under the Standard Measures protocol, dynamically comparing the active scenario's sleep duration against the 7.33-hour inflight cohort mean[cite: 1].

### Key Benefits & Expected Impact

* **Autonomous Onboard Triage:** Empowers astronauts on lunar or Mars missions to assess physiological trends and radiation indicators independently during Earth-link blackouts[cite: 1].

* **Elimination of False Medical Alarms:** Explicitly isolates sensor dropouts as State 06 ("Telemetry unavailable") with a clear warning that health status cannot be inferred, preventing crews from mistaking hardware failure for a medical emergency[cite: 1].

* **Auditability & Crew Trust:** Every state transition and operator acknowledgment is timestamped and exportable for post-blackout handoff to flight surgeons[cite: 1].

* **Zero-Infrastructure Portability:** Requires no cloud servers, external APIs, or installation, making it immediately deployable on isolated spacecraft workstations or analog field-mission tablets[cite: 1].

### Tools, Languages & Software Used

* **Core Technologies:** Built entirely with vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and modern JavaScript (ES6+) inside a single portable file (`COSMO-HEALTH.html`)[cite: 1].

* **Native Browser APIs:** Uses the HTML5 Canvas API for real-time 60-sample telemetry plotting, native `<dialog>` elements for the interactive guided tour, and Blob/URL APIs for client-side JSON and CSV data exports[cite: 1].

* **NASA Research & Challenge Frameworks:** Integrates published cohort statistics from NASA NTRS (`20230003916`) and aligns with NASA Standard Measures, NASA OSDR (Inspiration4 mission datasets), the NASA Human Research Program (HRP) spaceflight hazards framework, and CCMC DONKI space-weather concepts[cite: 1].

### How Our Project Is Creative

* **Epistemic Honesty in Interface Design:** Most health dashboards either freeze or display zero when a sensor disconnects; COSMO HEALTH elevates "unknown telemetry" into a dedicated operational state so crews always distinguish missing data from physiological risk[cite: 1].

* **Context-Aware Rule Evaluation:** Beyond static cutoffs, the rule engine weighs mission context—such as distinguishing elevated heart rate during an extravehicular activity (SCN-08) from a resting heart rate spike (SCN-06) or cumulative multi-night sleep debt (SCN-03)[cite: 1].

* **Interactive Guided Onboarding:** Includes a built-in 11-step interactive walkthrough (`Visite guidée`) that highlights live interface panels sequentially to train new crew members or evaluators in seconds[cite: 1].

### Factors Our Team Considered

* **Disconnection & Resilience:** Zero external scripts, fonts, or network requests ensure uninterrupted operation in offline environments[cite: 1].

* **Human Factors & Accessibility:** Designed with a low-glare dark interface, `tabular-nums` font alignment to prevent numeric jitter during live replay, ARIA live regions for screen-reader announcements, keyboard focus outlines, and `prefers-reduced-motion` support[cite: 1].

* **Scientific Transparency:** Clearly documents all prototype boundaries inside the interface, distinguishing illustrative rules and synthetic sensor fixtures from peer-reviewed NASA NTRS cohort benchmarks[cite: 1].
